about.title: Chowchilla Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Chowchilla's economy runs on agriculture, distribution, and the correctional facilities nearby, all of which carry real injury risk from heavy equipment, repetitive strain, and vehicle traffic. When a workplace injury happens, most employees assume workers' compensation is their only path forward, but that's not always the full picture. If a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, property owner, or another driver contributed to your injury, you may have a separate claim outside the workers' comp system entirely. This matters in a town where flatbed trucks, delivery vans, and farm vehicles regularly move along Robertson Boulevard and Trinity Avenue near work sites. Our team can review your specific situation and explain whether a third-party claim applies alongside your workers' comp benefits. There's no obligation to move forward, and no fee unless we recover something for you.

items.title: Workers' Comp Isn't Always the Whole Story
items.desc: California treats workers' comp as the exclusive remedy against your employer in most cases, but a negligent third party, like a subcontractor or equipment maker, can still be held separately liable.

items.title: Reporting Deadlines Move Fast
items.desc: You generally have 30 days to report a workplace injury to your employer, and missing that window can complicate your benefits, so early guidance matters.

items.title: Retaliation Is Illegal, and Deadlines Still Apply
items.desc: Your employer cannot legally punish you for reporting an injury, and if a third-party claim exists, California gives you two years to pursue it, so understanding your timeline early protects your options.

items.question: I was hurt at a job site near SR-99, does workers' comp cover everything?
items.answer: Workers' comp usually covers medical costs and lost wages regardless of fault, but it typically doesn't cover pain and suffering. If a third party, like a delivery driver or equipment supplier, contributed to the crash or incident, a separate claim may be available alongside your workers' comp benefits.

items.question: What if my employer discourages me from reporting my injury?
items.answer: Retaliation for reporting a workplace injury is illegal in California. If you're facing pressure not to report, we can advise you on protecting your rights while still meeting the 30-day reporting window.

items.question: Do you charge anything for a case review?
items.answer: No, the initial case review is free. We typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless we recover something for you.
